title: Creation of a Pre-biopsy Clinical Risk Score for Major Bleeding After Kidney Biopsy

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Creation of a Pre-biopsy Clinical Risk Score for Major Bleeding After Kidney Biopsy》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · abstract-1-1】Risk-based tools to guide care after percutaneous kidney biopsy (PKB) remain limited. We developed a simple preadmission risk score to predict post-PKB bleeding and support same-day discharge decisions, leveraging Japan's routine inpatient observation practice.

【Body · p0020】Several scoring systems to predict the risk of complications after PKB have been developed and validated,15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22 and many use clinically relevant prebiopsy information such as hemoglobin, platelet count, kidney size, comorbidities, and kidney function. These models have advanced individualized risk assessment and provided important tools for procedural decision-making. However, most existing tools were not specifically designed to support preadmission triage decisions. Although some previous risk models, including the nationwide French score developed by Halimi et al.,21 incorporated diagnosis-related categories, evidence remains limited regarding how preadmission clinical information available during outpatient evaluation can be translated into postbiopsy care pathways and discharge planning. Some conditions, such as systemic lupus erythematosus23 and amyloidosis,24 have been specifically investigated in relation to the risk of postbiopsy complications. Nonetheless, PKB is performed for a wide range of clinical conditions, including chronic glomerulonephritis, nephrotic syndrome, autoimmune diseases, and acute kidney injury, each of which may carry different baseline risks of bleeding. Furthermore, variability in reported complication rates, partly due to differences in outcome definitions and single- or multicenter cohorts,4, 6 makes the validation of scoring systems less straightforward.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Creation of a Pre-biopsy Clinical Risk Score for Major Bleeding After Kidney Biopsy》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Study Design and Data Source · p0030】This is a retrospective cohort study that analyzed data from the Diagnosis Procedure Combination inpatient database (2016–2021), a Japanese nationwide inpatient administrative database covering acute-care hospitalizations.25, 26, 27 It contains deidentified, admission-level information submitted by participating hospitals, including demographic characteristics, dates of admission and discharge, International Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th Revision (ICD-10)28 diagnosis codes, recorded comorbidities, procedures, prescribed drugs, discharge disposition, length of stay, and in-hospital outcomes. This study was approved by the ethics committee of the Institute of Science Tokyo (approval number M2000-788). Informed consent was waived because this retrospective study used anonymized data. The study was conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki and was reported in accordance with the STROBE guidelines for observational studies and the TRIPOD guidelines for clinical prediction model studies. Diagnosis Procedure Combination data cannot be shared; methodological details are available upon reasonable request.

【Data Collection and Patient Stratification · p0040】We collected data on age, sex, BMI, admission and discharge status, medications prescribed, comorbidities, and CCI,30 which is updated for risk adjustment.29, 31 Patients were stratified into 5 age groups based on their age (18–49, 50–59, 60–69, 70–79, and ≥ 80 years),32 and grouped into 4 BMI categories (< 18.5, 18.5–< 22.0, 22.0–< 25.0, and ≥ 25.0 kg/m2). The primary prebiopsy diagnosis was categorized into 10 clinically relevant groups based on ICD-10 codes (Figure 1 and Supplementary Table S1). Given that hemostatic agents are administered immediately before kidney biopsy in routine clinical practice in Japan, hemostatic medication use on the day of biopsy was identified using medication claims and categorized as follows: no agent used, tranexamic acid alone, carbazochrome sulfonate alone, and combination use. Of note, laboratory and imaging data were unavailable in our reimbursement claims-based database. Because guidelines in Japan recommend withholding antithrombotic agents for approximately 1 week before kidney biopsy,33 use of these agents was not included as a predictor in the present model.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Creation of a Pre-biopsy Clinical Risk Score for Major Bleeding After Kidney Biopsy》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · abstract-3-1】The overall bleeding rate was 1.46%. Compared with chronic glomerulonephritis, bleeding risk was higher in acute kidney injury (odds ratio [OR], 10.9; 95% confidence interval [CI], 8.55-13.9) and rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (OR, 6.67; 95% CI 5.48-8.12). Increasing age and lower body mass index (BMI) were independently associated with higher bleeding risk. Age, prebiopsy diagnostic risk tier, BMI, and Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) were selected for score construction (score range, 0-9). In the validation cohort, patients with scores ≤ 2 (55.4%) had a bleeding risk of 0.37%. Simulation analysis suggested that restricting early discharge to this low-risk group could reduce hospitalization by an estimated 332 hospital days per 100 patients while maintaining low postdischarge bleeding risk.

【Score Validation and Risk Stratification · p0110】The observed K-BIT scores for the validation cohort ranged from 0 to 8 (Supplementary Table S4). The scoring system demonstrated strong discriminatory ability; the event rate was 0.23% in the lowest score group (score 0) and gradually increased with higher scores (Supplementary Table S4). Nonbleeding patients showed a left-skewed distribution toward lower scores, whereas bleeding events clustered at higher scores (Figure 4b and c).

sections.text:

【Figure 1 · fig1】Figure 1 Flow diagram of patient selection. In total, 78,817 patients were included in the final analytic cohort. Patients were categorized into 10 clinical diagnostic groups based on admission diagnoses. AAV, antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody–associated vasculitis; BMI, body mass index; MGUS, monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance; MM, multiple myeloma; RPGN, rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis; SLE, systemic lupus erythematosus.

【Figure 2 · fig2】Figure 2 Incidence and timing of major bleeding events after percutaneous kidney biopsy. (a) Incidence of major bleeding events within the first 6 days after percutaneous kidney biopsy, stratified by age group (18–49, 50–59, 60–69, 70–79, and ≥80 years). (b) Distribution of the timing of major bleeding events according to postbiopsy day and age group. The z-axis represents the percentage of events within each age category. Most events occurred on the day of (day 0) and the day after (day 1) the biopsy. Green, 18–49 years; light green, 50–59 years; yellow, 60–69 years; pink, 70–79 years; red, ≥ 80 years.

【Figure 3 · fig3】Figure 3 Adjusted odds ratios for major bleeding events. Forest plots showing adjusted ORs and 95% CIs for major bleeding events across different risk factors: (a) Age group (reference: 18–49 years); (b) body mass index (BMI) categories (reference: < 18.5 kg/m2); (c) prebiopsy clinical diagnosis categories (reference: chronic glomerulonephritis); and (d) use of hemostatic agents (reference: none). The logistic regression model was adjusted for year of biopsy, age group, sex, BMI, CCI, use of hemostatic agents, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and prebiopsy clinical diagnostic category. AAV, antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody–associated vasculitis; AKI, acute kidney injury; ARF, acute renal failure; BMI, body mass index; CGN, chronic glomerulonephritis; CI, confidence interval; MGUS, monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance; MM, multiple myeloma; OR, odds ratio; RPGN, rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis; SLE, systemic lupus erythematosus.

sections.title: 复现线索
sections.text:
《Creation of a Pre-biopsy Clinical Risk Score for Major Bleeding After Kidney Biopsy》：复现时可直接核对的数据、软件或实现线索。

【Data Availability Statement · p0185】The individual-level data used in this study cannot be made publicly available because of restrictions related to the use of the Diagnosis Procedure Combination database in Japan. Analytical code and model specifications may be made available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request, subject to institutional approval and data-use restrictions. Supplementary material is available online.

【Statistical Analysis · p0065】Internal validation was performed using an independent test cohort derived from the same dataset covering 2 Japanese regions (Chugoku/Shikoku: 9007 [11.43%], Kyushu/Okinawa: 10,615 [13.47%]; total n = 19,622; Supplementary Figure S1). For comparison with conventional binary outcome evaluation, we additionally performed a binary receiver operating characteristic analysis. The multiple bleeding-timing categories were combined into a binary outcome: any bleeding event versus no bleeding. The predicted probability of any bleeding event was calculated by summing the predicted probabilities across all bleeding categories. Model discrimination for any bleeding event was assessed using the area under the curve (AUC, with 95% confidence intervals calculated by DeLong’s method). Analyses were conducted using JMP Pro 17.0 (SAS Institute Inc., Cary, NC, USA), Stata version 18.0 (Stata Corp, College Station, TX, USA), and R version 4.5.0 (R Foundation for Statistical Computing, Vienna, Austria). A 2-sided P value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
